questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡(6x-\frac{\pi }{4})=1
$$

  

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=a\pi +\frac{n\pi }{6},
$$

 
where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the range $[0,\frac{1}{6}).$

$a=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-\frac{\pi }{4} & =\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the above equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6x & =\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi  \\ 6x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a=\frac{1}{12}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡(5x+{75}^{∘})=-1
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x={a}^{∘}+n\cdot {36}^{∘},
$$

 
where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value $a$ in the range $[{0}^{∘},{36}^{∘}).$

$a=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
questions.worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+{75}^{∘} & ={135}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the above equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & ={135}^{∘}-{75}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ 5x & ={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ x & ={12}^{∘}+n\cdot {36}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a=12.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Reciprocal Function
questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(6x+{12}^{∘})=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}
$$

  

The general solution of this equation is

$$
x={8}^{∘}+{60}^{∘}\cdot n,\,x=a+{60}^{∘}\cdot n,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the range $[{0}^{∘},{60}^{∘}).$

$a=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x+{12}^{∘})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
6x+{12}^{∘}={60}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n,\,6x+{12}^{∘}={120}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n.
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6x & ={60}^{∘}-{12}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n, & \,6x & ={120}^{∘}-{12}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n \\ 6x & ={48}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n, & \,6x & ={108}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n \\ x & ={8}^{∘}+{60}^{∘}\cdot n, & \,x & ={18}^{∘}+{60}^{∘}\cdot n.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a={18}^{∘}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Reciprocal Function
questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation:

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{4})=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=a\pi +4\pi n,\,x=-\frac{7\pi }{6}+4\pi n,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the range $(-4,0].$

$a=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{4})=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{4}=-\frac{2\pi }{3}+2\pi n,\,\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{4}=-\frac{\pi }{3}+2\pi n.
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & =-\frac{2\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}+2\pi n, & \, & \frac{x}{2}=-\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}+2\pi n \\ \frac{x}{2} & =-\frac{11\pi }{12}+2\pi n, & \, & \frac{x}{2}=-\frac{7\pi }{12}+2\pi n \\ x & =-\frac{11\pi }{6}+4\pi n, & \, & x=-\frac{7\pi }{6}+4\pi n.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have that $a=-\frac{11}{6}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to an Equation Containing a Transformed Cosine Function
questions.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3x}{2})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{4\pi n}{3},\,x=a\pi +\frac{4\pi n}{3},
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the interval $[0,\frac{4}{3}).$

$a=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{4}+2\pi n, & \, & \, & \frac{3x}{2} & =\frac{7\pi }{4}+2\pi n.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{4}+2\pi n & \, & \, & \frac{3x}{2} & =\frac{7\pi }{4}+2\pi n \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{4\pi n}{3} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{7\pi }{6}+\frac{4\pi n}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a=\frac{7}{6}.$
